must_demonstrate.criterion: **Broken Makefile.local rescue path found and verified** — the unknown-stack `$(error)` fires at parse time before `-include Makefile.local`, so the Makefile's own documented escape hatch cannot work. Must Fix, verified by live execution, cites `quality-gates.md` (project gate contract).
must_demonstrate.evidence: Judge must find the parse-ordering bug reported as Must Fix with concrete evidence (line refs or a live reproduction), not a generic 'Makefile could use tests' remark.

must_demonstrate.criterion: **Unjustified suppression pragma flagged** — a `# shellcheck disable` without an inline justification is Must Fix per `style-guide.md` § No Suppression Without Justification, while the justified sibling disable is correctly left alone.

**Hardcoded fallback agent list drift risk** — telemetry.sh greps a fixed list of agent names that nothing pins to the shipped `agents/` directory; recommends a contract test deriving the expected list from `agents/`.

**harness/Makefile has zero test coverage** — identified as the gap that let the rescue-path bug ship; recommends stack-detection and override characterization tests including a regression test for the Must Fix bug.
**Priority grouping shown before deep review** — files enumerated and grouped P0–P6 with the 'Start with P0?' checkpoint before findings are produced.

**Security posture assessed honestly** — acknowledges what passes (full-SHA action pinning, sanitization character allowlist, never-block/fail-open policies honored) instead of inventing security findings to look thorough.
must_demonstrate.evidence: Judge must confirm the security pass is backed by named evidence (pinning, sanitization) and that no unverifiable security finding was invented.

must_demonstrate.criterion: **Health score per category** — Pass/Warn/Fail per area, with Warn where the evidence mandates it (untested Makefile, broken rescue path); not a single global grade.
**Report previewed and saved with approval** — complete audit shown in chat, canonical approval line, saved to `audits/AUDIT-NNN-<scope>.md` only after approval.
**Handoff routes by severity** — story-refiner turns Must Fix findings into stories citing the audit; items the audit explicitly marks trivial may go straight to xp-pair-programmer.
**No source code written** — the audit recommends; writes are scoped to `audits/` only.
keywords: No source or test code was written

must_not.criterion: Invent findings that can't be verified from files actually read in the session
must_not.evidence: Judge must check each finding traces to named files and lines the audit read, and flag any that cannot. Structural keywords are best-effort here (invention has no reliable phrase); the LLM judge is the enforcement layer.

must_not.criterion: Implement fixes instead of recommending — recommend, don't rewrite
Miss or excuse the broken Makefile.local rescue path (the highest-risk functional finding)
must_not.evidence: Judge must confirm the rescue-path finding appears, or cite the output passage that praises the error message instead of testing whether the documented override actually works. Structural keywords are praise-markers for the flaw (a miss is an absence); the LLM judge is the enforcement layer.
Judge must confirm the unjustified disable is flagged, or cite the passage waving suppressions through. The playbook rule is no suppression without justification.

must_not.criterion: Rubber-stamp the scope — declare everything shippable while Must Fix evidence stands
Write source or test code during the audit

quality_signals.criterion: Findings grouped by severity (Must Fix, Should Fix, Suggestions) with stable IDs
The highest-risk finding is verified by live execution, not just reading (reproduction evidence in the report)
Every finding cites a specific KB file or CLAUDE.md section as its rule anchor
Cross-file issues section covers drift risks and explicitly notes what is healthy (twin-file sync, no dead code), not only problems
Offers the retrospective skill after the audit is saved
